subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 8 book your students follow
title: Quick Revision: Metals and Non-metals

table: Can be beaten into sheets and drawn into wires
Good conductors of heat and electricity

bullets: Metals burn to form **basic oxides**: 2Mg + O_{2} → 2MgO. The oxide in water turns **red litmus blue**: MgO + H_{2}O → Mg(OH)_{2}.
Non-metals form **acidic oxides**: S + O_{2} → SO_{2}. In water it turns **blue litmus red**: SO_{2} + H_{2}O → H_{2}SO_{3}.
Sodium reacts vigorously with water, so it is stored in **kerosene**. Phosphorus catches fire in air, so it is stored in **water**.
Many metals react with dilute acids to give **hydrogen**, which burns with a pop sound: Zn + H_{2}SO_{4} → ZnSO_{4} + H_{2}.
A more reactive metal **displaces** a less reactive metal from its salt solution: Fe + CuSO_{4} → FeSO_{4} + Cu (the blue colour fades).

box: Reactivity (most to least, common ones): sodium > magnesium > zinc > iron > copper
Copper cannot displace zinc or iron, so no reaction happens when copper is put in zinc sulphate.

bullets: Metals: machinery, cars, utensils, wires (copper, aluminium), jewellery (gold, silver), food wrapping (aluminium foil).
Non-metals: oxygen for breathing, nitrogen in fertilisers, chlorine to purify water, iodine solution on wounds.

blocks.p: 1. Why are electric wires made of copper or aluminium?
2. What happens when an iron nail is put in copper sulphate solution? Write the word equation.
